name: L-system arbor
note: A stochastic bracketed L-system (Prusinkiewicz & Lindenmayer) is rewritten n times and read by a turtle into a segment hierarchy; widths follow the pipe model, growth runs along path length, and every frame re-poses the tree with flex-weighted wind and tropism, while a season slider turns and drops the leaves.

name: Gray-Scott morphogen
note: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion on a toroidal grid with Karl Sims' nine-point Laplacian, stepped a dozen times a frame and shaded as relief from the gradient of V; a feed/kill pad plots Pearson's regimes against the saddle-node curve k = sqrt(F)/2 - F, and the brush drops fresh catalyst.

name: Voronoi stipple study
note: Secord's weighted Voronoi stippling: every frame each dot moves to the density-weighted centroid of its Voronoi cell (one Lloyd step, nearest-dot search on a uniform grid), over a density raster ray-cast from seeded ellipsoid pebbles with Lambert shading, cast shadows and contact occlusion under a movable sun.

name: Subdivision quilt
note: Recursive subdivision built from real nested CSS grids (fr tracks at thirds, halves and golden cuts), so the composition reflows with its container; each panel is a size container whose motif is drawn with gradients steered by a registered <angle>, so turns and hovers spring through CSS trig.

name: Phased array interference
note: Wave interference from a seeded phased array: each element's phasor e^{ikr}/sqrt(r) is cached per cell, so steering is one complex multiply per element and the travelling field is Re(S e^{-iwt}); the array factor is evaluated around the circle for the -3 dB beamwidth and grating lobes, and drawn as a polar trace.

name: Contour survey sheet
note: Domain-warped fbm with a ridged octave becomes a slowly breathing height field; marching squares traces every contour in one pass per cell, index contours carry upright labels pinned to fixed anchors so they glide rather than jump, and a water slider floods the valleys with offset waterlines.

name: Differential growth
note: Differential growth on closed curves: every node is pulled toward its neighbours' rest length and midpoint and pushed off any node within the fold radius (uniform-grid search), while new nodes split long edges and sprout where the pointer feeds them; the outline is stamped every half second into agate-like growth rings.
